title: Ribbon Translation: Contextual Side Rail & Workspace Routing Reframe
creator: Arjun Patel
description: Problem: Console navigation is fragmented across a legacy left rail, ephemeral top routes, and disparate workspace switchers. Users testing multi-workspace flows frequently lose context when switching between dashboards, rollouts, and cost views. Goal: Reframe navigation as a single ribbon + contextual side rail that adapts to the active workspace and surface the most relevant console routes (dashboards, rollouts, cost lenses) with clear hierarchy and predictable routing. This ticket covers low-fidelity -> high-fidelity prototypes, cross-functional reviews, and a path to an A/B rollout with telemetry hooks.
updates: 2026-02-20: Ticket created — kickoff doc and problem framing added to PRD. Identified primary user journeys: dashboard -> rollout -> cost review, and switch-to-workspace scenarios for platform teams.
2026-02-25: Sketches validated with PM & Eng — consensus to test a horizontal ribbon for global routes and a contextual side rail for workspace-scoped tools (rollouts, evals, cost breakdown).
2026-03-02: Mid-fidelity prototype completed (Figma). Linked prototypes for desktop and narrow-screen adaptivity. Edge-case: long workspace names and many pinned routes — discussed overflow handling.

2026-03-05: Cross-functional design review with Product, Runtime Eng, and Frontend — Eng asked for explicit routing contract and rollback plan; Product requested telemetry to measure workspace-switch drop-offs.
2026-03-08: Usability test (n=8 engineers/product folks) — 6/8 completed task flows faster than baseline, confusion remained around pinning vs. temporary tabs. Added microcopy and affordance changes.
2026-03-10: GH PR opened for initial CSS/layout and route-handler shim (PR #1284). Engineering notes inline in PR about route canonicalization and preserving deep links.
2026-03-12: Preparing for design review sign-off; created rollout plan and telemetry checklist for A/B experiment.
design_decisions: Adopt a hybrid navigation: horizontal ribbon for cross-workspace global contexts + contextual side rail for active workspace tools.
Preserve existing route URLs; introduce a routing layer that maps ribbon state to canonical routes to avoid breaking external links.
Workspace switcher moves to the left of the ribbon with a compact avatar + name chip — clicking opens transient workspace drawer rather than full page navigation.
Cost views are surfaced as a first-class route under the workspace side rail with two entry points: global cost lens (ribbon) and workspace cost breakdown (side rail).
Primary CTA styles standardized across ribbon and side rail for rollouts: .cta-primary for start canary, .cta-secondary for view history.
Accessibility: ensure ribbon is keyboard-traversable and maintains focus when workspace drawer opens.
Mobile: ribbon collapses into compact overflow menu; side rail becomes an in-page sticky toolbar.
Fallback: on capacity or compatibility issues revert to existing left rail using feature-flag toggle tied to release channel.
tradeoffs: Tradeoff: horizontal ribbon increases top chrome and reduces vertical space for dashboards; mitigated by allowing users to collapse the ribbon (persisted preference).
Tradeoff: canonical route mapping adds routing complexity but preserves deep links and SEO for embedded dashboards. Engineering accepts additional router shim.
Tradeoff: exposing cost lenses prominently may increase accidental queries; added confirmation and rate-limited backend endpoints to avoid cost spikes.
Tradeoff: workspace drawer introduces transient UI state which may confuse keyboard-only users; addressed with focus management and clear aria-live announcements.
Tradeoff: rollout gating requires both frontend feature flag and runtime support in backend routing; dependency on ENG-67021 for backend routing shim.
Tradeoff: A/B rollout will require more telemetry instrumentation up-front which slows initial deployment but yields clearer measurement for iteration.
review_feedback: PM (Liam O'Neill): pleased with reduced cognitive load when switching tasks; asked for clearer error states when a workspace is missing permissions.
Eng (Priya Kapoor): requested explicit routing contract and a migration plan for deep links. Suggested adding integration tests for route equivalence.
Security (Noah Ramirez): confirmed no new sensitive surfaces introduced but flagged that Workspace drawer must respect RBAC checks before rendering list items.
Design review panel: asked to run a short guerilla test with external customers and to prototype sticky-collapsed ribbon state.
Accessibility reviewer (Sofia Martinez): requested better focus ring contrast and announced landmarks for ribbon/side-rail regions.
user_testing_summary: Method: remote moderated sessions (n=8), tasks centered on switching to a pinned rollout and viewing workspace cost breakdown.
Key finding: users completed tasks 25% faster on average vs baseline and reported higher confidence in locating rollout controls.
Pain point: confusion between pinning a route to ribbon vs adding to workspace favorites; added distinct pin iconography and tooltip copy.
Edge behavior: users with >12 pinned items reached overflow — implemented a contextual overflow menu and search within ribbon.
Net Promoter: informal feedback improved, with external customers asking for the same pattern on mobile web.
next_steps: Finalize Figma high-fidelity screens with updated microcopy (due 2026-03-18).
Ship frontend feature-flagged rollout with router shim and telemetry hooks (coordinate with ENG-67021).
Eng to add integration tests for route canonicalization and deep-link preservation (PR #1284 references).
Run controlled A/B experiment with 10% of org traffic, measure task completion, drop-offs, and cost-query rates over 2 weeks.
Collect customer feedback via Solutions Eng pilot and refine pinning affordance.
Confirm accessibility audit and security RBAC checks before wide rollout.
